properties.note: Productive pre-reaction complex and lowest verified B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-SVP malonic acid minimum (0 imaginary frequencies, normal termination): intramolecularly H-bonded six-membered-ring rotamer with the C5 hydroxyl proton H11 pointing at the C2 carbonyl oxygen O1 (O1...H11 = 1.749 A). Both the RC node and the step-1 barrier reference. Other verified malonic-acid conformers: sp/ma_dhb_optfreq.log (-417.357122930), sp/rc_chel_optfreq.log (-417.354040611). Atom indices in bond_changes are task atom-map indices: O1=C2(O3-H8)-C4H2-C5(=O6)(O7-H11). Reproduced as the reactant-side endpoint of the step-1 IRC (ts/ts_0001/jobs/declaration_0021/reactant_opt/reactant_opt.log, -417.360029532 Ha and 0 imaginary frequencies), so the barrier reference and the IRC reactant endpoint are the same minimum.

Concerted six-membered-ring saddle (O1...H11-O7-C5-C4-C2): proton transfer H11->O1 synchronous with C4-C5 cleavage and C5=O7 double-bond formation. Exactly one imaginary frequency, -409.46 cm^-1; geometry at the saddle: O1-H11 1.03, O7-H11 1.54, C4-C5 1.99, C2-O1 1.30, C2-C4 1.40, C5-O6 1.23, C5-O7 1.22 A. Barrier 27.96 kcal/mol vs RC.

Ethene-1,1-diol (enol of acetic acid) hydrogen bonded to CO2. This node carries the LOWEST verified minimum of the enol state: the forward outer frame of the step-1 IRC (ts/ts_0001/jobs/declaration_0019/irc/irc.log) was optimized and frequency-checked (sp/irc_fwd_endpoint_optfreq.log, Stationary point found, 0 imaginary frequencies, C2=C4 1.345, C2-O1 1.353 with O1-H11 0.970, C2-O3 1.344 with O3-H8 0.968, separate CO2 C5-O6 1.158 / C5-O7 1.168, H11...O7 2.047 A). Other verified enol conformers: -417.330500124 (ts/ts_0002/jobs/declaration_0005/reactant_frequency/reactant_frequency.log, the geometry the step-2 IRC itself reaches, +1.11 kcal/mol) and -417.328172393 (sp/im_optfreq_v3.log, +2.58 kcal/mol). The step-2 barrier is quoted against the lowest minimum, i.e. this node. Confirmed independently by the workflow's own endpoint work on the normally terminated short IRC (ts/ts_0001/jobs/declaration_0021/product_frequency/product_frequency.log, -417.332272549 Ha, 0 imaginary frequencies), which reproduces the same enol minimum to 2e-6 Ha.

1,3-H shift (four-membered ring O3-C2=C4) converting the enol into the keto acid; CO2 is a spectator. First-order saddle: optimization converged to a stationary point, exactly one imaginary frequency at -2062.43 cm^-1, normal termination. Barrier 46.40 kcal/mol vs the Enol Intermediate node (-417.332274286 Ha), i.e. the higher of the two declared barriers; measured against the enol conformer the step-2 IRC actually reaches (-417.330500124) it is 45.28 kcal/mol, the difference being the 1.11 kcal/mol conformer offset.

Acetic acid + CO2 complex, as actually reached by the step-2 IRC: the TS2 forward outer frame was optimized (ts/ts_0002/jobs/declaration_0005/product_opt/product_opt.log, Stationary point found, same energy) and frequency-checked (0 imaginary frequencies, normal termination); this is the syn conformer of the acetic acid O-H. A previously verified conformer with the O-H pointing away from its own C=O (anti, O...O to CO2 2.46 A), sp/pc_optfreq.log (-417.367422563), lies 5.58 kcal/mol higher and is kept as a documented conformer datum.

edges.note: Concerted six-membered-ring step: H11 transfers from O7 to the C2 carbonyl oxygen O1, C4-C5 cleaves, C5-O7 rises to a double bond (CO2 formed) and C2-C4 rises from single to double (C2=C4 1.508 A in the reactant -> 1.398 A at TS1 -> 1.346 A in the enol), giving ethene-1,1-diol + CO2. C5-O6 and C2-O3 do not change order. Barrier 27.96 kcal/mol vs Reactant Complex -417.360029462 (E(TS1) -417.315470357).

DeltaE(double dagger) = E(TS2) - E(IM, lowest verified enol minimum sp/irc_fwd_endpoint_optfreq.log) = -417.258335918 - (-417.332274286) Ha = 46.40 kcal/mol, electronic only (no ZPE). (Measured against the enol conformer the step-2 IRC actually reaches, -417.330500124, the same barrier is 45.28 kcal/mol; the difference is the 1.11 kcal/mol conformer offset.) The unimolecular 1,3-H shift is the higher barrier of the network, so at this level it would be rate-determining and the enol would remain metastable; an assisted (CO2- or second-molecule-mediated) tautomerization is expected to lower it.

notes_alternative_channels.note: Assigned eight-membered channel (ring O1-H11-O7-C5-C4-H8-O3-C2; break C4-C5, C2=O1, O7-H11; form O1-H11, C5=O7, C4-H8, C2=O3) tested with the user's geometry recipe (TS1 geometry with H8 moved to O3-H8 1.520 A / C4-H8 1.500 A, C4-C5 1.990 A, ring closed), one ts_prepare run (ts/ts_0005) after fixing the automatic atom map (candidate 0 had encoded the four-membered H11->C4 product; selected_candidate=10 encodes the assigned bond changes). RESULT, log-backed: the assigned CONCERTED one-elementary-step decarboxylation is NOT supported. The converged first-order saddle (-417.260736202 Ha, one imaginary mode -1991.2 cm^-1, +62.31 kcal/mol from the Reactant Complex) has C4-C5 already broken (3.198 A) and the eight-membered ring open, and its imaginary mode is 94.5% H8 motion (heavy-atom fraction 0.007): it is the O3-H8 -> C4 tautomerisation of the acetic-acid fragment AFTER CO2 loss, barrier 43.79 kcal/mol from its own enediol minimum (-417.330522382, enediol + CO2), i.e. an unassigned post-decarboxylation step rather than the assigned concerted step. The workflow verdict is candidate_only / verified=false because its source slot perceived C=C(O)O.O=C=O, not the malonic-acid reactant - reported as it stands, not overridden. Together with the non-converged first attempt (declaration 0002, last SCF -417.260733066 Ha, +62.3 kcal/mol) the record shows: the optimiser repeatedly breaks C4-C5 before any H8 delivery, so decarboxylation and H8 migration separate into two steps at this level. No barrier is declared for the assigned concerted channel and it is not a competing route on the available evidence; what the calculation does NOT show is that no such saddle exists anywhere on the PES.

remaining_gaps: Assisted (bimolecular) tautomerisation of the enol was NOT computed: a second carboxylic acid (malonic acid, 22 atoms, or the acetic acid product, 19 atoms) shuttling O3-H8 to C4 would remove the strained four-membered 1,3-H shift of TS2. Costed at roughly 5-8 h (19-atom) to 8-12 h (22-atom) of B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-SVP work including retries, which exceeded the remaining budget. It is the one calculation that could bring the network's effective barrier down to the 27.96 kcal/mol decarboxylation step and it is the recommended next step.

The unimolecular network delivered here has an effective barrier of 63.81 kcal/mol from the Reactant Complex via TS2 (46.40 kcal/mol above the Enol Intermediate). That is incompatible with gas-phase thermolysis at 150-200 C, so the delivered mechanism must be read as the verified elementary-step network at this level of theory, not as a quantitative explanation of the experimental rate.
NO solvent, counterion or pressure dependence is modelled (gas phase, isolated molecules, charge 0, multiplicity 1).

NO ZPE, thermal or entropy corrections are applied: every barrier in this graph is a purely electronic DeltaE, and the temperature-dependent preference between channels could shift once free energies are included.

Barrier references are single lowest verified minima per state. Conformer spread on the malonic-acid side is 1.8-3.8 kcal/mol (sp/ma_dhb_optfreq.log -417.357122930, sp/rc_chel_optfreq.log -417.354040611) and the enol state has at least three verified minima (-417.332274286 lowest, -417.330500124 +1.11, -417.328172393 +2.58).

The CO2-containing complexes (enol + CO2 and acetic acid + CO2) are shallow minima with very low librational modes (33-45 cm^-1), so their relative energies are more method-sensitive than the covalent saddle energies.
